gaps.sentence: She was elected ___ president of the students' union.
gaps.explanation: After 'elect/appoint/make + role', the article is usually dropped: elected president.

gaps.sentence: He ordered ___ steak, but it arrived cold.
gaps.explanation: 'A steak' first, then 'the waiter' — the restaurant's waiter, definite in context.
Single mountain peaks take no article: Everest, Mont Blanc (compare: the Alps).

gaps.sentence: He was wearing ___ strange metal bracelet on his left wrist.
gaps.explanation: 'A strange bracelet' (first mention); body parts after prepositions traditionally take 'the' (on the left wrist).

gaps.sentence: She spent three weeks in ___ hospital after the accident.
gaps.explanation: British English: be in hospital (as a patient) takes no article; the building is the hospital.

gaps.sentence: It was ___ honour to meet the ambassador.
gaps.explanation: 'Honour' starts with a vowel sound (silent h), so 'an honour'.

gaps.sentence: He earns fifty thousand pounds ___ year.
gaps.explanation: 'Fifty thousand a year' — 'a' = per in rates.

gaps.sentence: She earns her living as ___ journalist.
gaps.explanation: Jobs after 'as' take a/an: as a journalist.
